findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving MySQL a public endpoint resolvable from the internet and removing the VPC network boundary as a control. Only the security group stands between the master 'admin' account and untrusted networks.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS volume and its snapshots, leaving stored catalog data unprotected on disk and in any snapshot copies.

The attached parameter group sets only character set parameters; require_secure_transport is not enabled, so the publicly reachable MySQL endpoint accepts unencrypted client connections, permitting cleartext transmission of credentials and query data.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". This role is attached through aws_iam_instance_profile.catalog_app_profile to an internet-facing web server, so compromise of the PHP application yields near-total control of S3, EC2 and RDS in the account, enabling data exfiltration and privilege escalation.

The user_data script interpolates the RDS master username and var.password into a PHP include file. User data is stored unencrypted in instance metadata (retrievable via IMDS or by any local process/SSRF) and in Terraform state, leaking the database master credential.

No metadata_options block is configured, so IMDSv1 remains available. Combined with the wildcard IAM role, a server-side request forgery or application flaw in the PHP app can be used to harvest role credentials.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the root volume holding /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc with the plaintext database password may be created unencrypted.

The bootstrap installs and starts httpd serving a PHP form over plain HTTP with no TLS configuration, and the instance's public DNS is exported, so submitted employee data traverses the network in cleartext.
Egress from the database security group allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, giving a compromised database endpoint an unrestricted outbound channel for exfiltration or callback.

Ingress on 3306 is permitted from the entire VPC CIDR rather than only the application server's security group, so every workload in the VPC can reach the database directly; this is the sole control protecting a publicly_accessible instance.
